name: Stollen
origin: Christstollen, from Dresden, Germany, since at least the 15th century; a yeasted, enriched fruit bread rather than a chemically leavened cake, dusted heavily with icing sugar, its shape traditionally said to represent the swaddled infant of the Nativity.

ingredients.note: rum used to soak the dried fruit before mixing, contributing a little of the dough's own liquid

stollen is yeast-leavened, not chemically leavened; bakersPercent here represents a nominal yeast inoculation rate rather than a bicarbonate dose, and physically belongs to the fermentation chemistry in leavening.ts (fermentGlucose), not the bicarbonate reaction validateFormulation's leavening ceiling is calibrated against — flagged for future work rather than pretending otherwise

process.name: mix and knead dough
process.description: mix flour, milk, egg, sugar, salt and yeast into a dough, then knead in the softened butter

process.name: fold in fruit
process.description: fold in the rum-soaked dried fruit

notes: A representative German enriched-dough proportion: substantial butter (65% of flour) and dried fruit (70%) relative to a fairly modest sugar dose (icing sugar dusted on after baking, out of scope here, does most of stollen's real sweetening). See the leavening-role note above for why a yeasted dough's leavening figure is only a nominal placeholder in this formulation engine today.
